Subject: Post-call: FinTechCo performance SLOs & VPC/peering follow-up

Hi Samuel — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we have alignment before the PoC kickoff:

Summary of goals and constraints:
- Target p95 latency for text-generation requests: <= 200 ms (end-to-end for 512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: ~250 qps across 8 concurrent clients (burst to 400 qps)
- Streaming behavior: need chunked streaming with first-byte latency < 80 ms and steady-state chunk latency < 40 ms
- Deployment: Private/VPC deployment in your AWS account (preferred) or VPC peering; potential on-prem option later

Network items we need to qualify today:
1) Network path: will you prefer VPC peering (AWS VPC Peering/Transit Gateway) or a VPN/Direct Connect approach?
2) Egress path & NAT: any corporate egress that will add hairpinning/NAT? If so, what's typical added latency (ms)?
3) Peering CIDR(s) and proposed AZ/region for the PoC (we recommended us-west-2 during the call)
4) Any MTU/packet inspection devices, TCP proxy/load balancers (e.g., F5, Palo Alto) that might impact streaming/TCP window behavior

Attached is a draft SLO matrix and a simple PoC checklist (redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx, poc-checklist.md). Next steps (proposed):
- Samuel: confirm network approach (peering vs VPN), provide infra POC and a basic network diagram (CIDRs, NAT/egress path) — by EOD Fri 13 Mar
- Dev (solutions eng): we'll run an iPerf test guidance and provide a short validation script for chunked streaming measurements
- Marissa/Aditya: schedule PoC kickoff for week of 23 Mar and agree success criteria

If you want, we can also run a short 30-min tech session with your infra team to walk the diagram and test plan.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — good notes. A few quick answers from the infra side:

1) Peering vs VPN: our preference is to start with VPC Peering/Transit Gateway to minimize extra hops. We have Transit Gateway in us-west-2.
2) Egress/NAT: our current setup uses a centralized NAT gateway in a shared services VPC for outbound traffic. Typical internal latency to shared services NAT is ~10-15 ms; additional hairpin could add 20-30 ms depending on route. We'll confirm exact path.
3) CIDRs/region: we'll plan us-west-2 for the PoC. Attaching a basic network diagram internally (we'll push a cleaned copy to you).
4) MTU/proxies: we have a few Palo Alto filters and one F5 in front of some internal services; they shouldn't be on the direct peering path but will confirm.

POC POC: I'm putting Chris Kim on the thread (infra owner) and he'll be the technical POC. He'll respond with the diagram and any constraints by tomorrow.

Samuel Park

Hi all — thanks for the details, Samuel. A few technical notes from the Redwood side that will help the PoC and prevent surprises:

Network/transport guidance:
- We recommend VPC peering/Transit Gateway in us-west-2 to minimize extra hops. Direct Connect can be considered later for steady-state production.
- Ports: outbound 443 (TLS) is sufficient; ensure egress rules allow persistent TLS sessions to Redwood endpoints.
- Keepalive/TCP tuning: recommend TCP keepalive ~60s and idle time > 300s to avoid intermediate NAT timeouts.
- MTU: 1500 standard OK; if you have jumbo frames in the path let us know.
- Proxies/inspection: any TLS-terminating proxy will disrupt end-to-end streaming; if proxies inspect TLS, we should schedule a test and test with chunked responses.

Performance validation plan:
1) iPerf / ping tests between a temporary test host in your PoC VPC and a Redwood test endpoint (we'll provide IPs) — capture baseline RTT and jitter.
2) Simulated load: we'll run a load script that mimics your concurrency (8 clients, ramp to 50 clients) and measure p50/p95/p99 request latencies and streaming-first-byte times.
3) Packet capture: short tcpdump sessions to check re-transmits and MTU issues during streaming.

PoC resource ask (minimal):
- A small EC2 instance in your PoC VPC (t3.medium or comparable) to run iPerf and the load script
- Security group allowing outbound TLS to Redwood test IPs and inbound SSH from your infra team
- Contact for Transit Gateway peering config (we can share CloudFormation snippets if you want)

I'll attach a short script and iperf guidance after I confirm some internal test IPs. Happy to do a 30-min tech sync with Chris.

- Dev
